recommendation: Aeroflow Systems at INR 47,20,000 normalized — not Cooltech, despite Cooltech's INR 39,83,000 headline.
conditions: Cooltech confirming in writing whether its excluded installation scope can be priced; if it lands materially below INR 5,20,000 the ranking is live again.
Both Aeroflow and Nordic correcting the arithmetic errors in their own stated totals before any award.
The AHU make being locked in the order — 'equivalent approved' is not a specification.

diagnosis.quantum: explains INR 5,20,000, 70.6% of the gap to Aeroflow
diagnosis.evidence: Cooltech excludes installation, commissioning and testing & balancing (p.2: 'Technical supervision during client-arranged erection'); Aeroflow and Nordic both include them. Cooltech is not INR 7,37,000 cheaper — it is cheaper by whatever erection costs minus INR 85,000.
diagnosis.action: Obtain Cooltech's installed price, or a firm quote from an erection contractor, before comparing anything else.

diagnosis.quantum: likely explains INR 2,68,000, 36.4% of the gap; medium confidence
diagnosis.evidence: Aeroflow and Nordic name a premium make; Cooltech states only 'equivalent approved'. Inferred from the price pattern across the equipment line, not from a stated specification — no vendor supplied a make/model sheet.
diagnosis.action: Lock the make and model in the tender and re-price. This is the single highest-yield question available.

diagnosis.quantum: moves INR 2,08,000 the other way, -28.2% of the gap
diagnosis.evidence: Cooltech's chilled water piping is INR 2,750/rm against INR 2,100 and INR 2,050 from the other two — 19.6% above the cross-vendor mean on an identically-described line.
diagnosis.action: Cooltech is low on equipment and high on piping. Ask for rate justification; if quantities grow on site, this rate is where the money leaves.

diagnosis.quantum: Aeroflow overstates by INR 78,000; Nordic understates by INR 1,10,000
diagnosis.evidence: Both vendors' grand totals disagree with the sum of their own line items. Recomputed from their rates and quantities.
diagnosis.action: Raise before negotiating anything else. Which figure they stand behind changes the comparison.

diagnosis.quantum: not in the price, material to value
diagnosis.evidence: Cooltech asks 50% advance with 12-month warranty and a 15-day validity carrying an escalation clause. Nordic asks 20% advance with 36-month warranty and 60-day validity. Aeroflow sits between.
diagnosis.action: Price the warranty gap over the horizon. Cooltech's 15-day validity plus escalation clause is a repricing option held against you on a 70-day lead time.

diagnosis.evidence: No vendor supplied a cost build-up and no benchmark file was provided. Any claim about which vendor is carrying more margin would be invented.
diagnosis.action: Request rate analysis for the top three lines by value. Refusal is itself informative.

next_actions: Issue the ask-list to all three vendors with a common response deadline and a fixed response format.
Lock the AHU make and model before re-pricing; re-tender that line only.
Obtain Cooltech's installed price or drop them from the comparison — as quoted they are answering a different question.
Get both arithmetic mismatches confirmed in writing.
Re-run the comparison once responses land; the residual is zero now, so any movement will be traceable to a specific line.
